nodes.summary: For every natural number $p$, $\sum_{n=0}^{p} n\, D(n) = \lfloor (p + 1)!/e \rfloor$, where $D(n)$ is the number of derangements of $n$ objects.

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be integers with $n \ge 1$ and $1 \le k \le n$. Call a permutation of an $n$-element set cyclic when it has exactly one cycle, fixed points counted as cycles. Write $c(n+1, k)$ for the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind, the number of permutations of $n + 1$ elements with exactly $k$ cycles.
